title: Our Solar System
intro: Blast off on a tour of the Sun, the Moon and the eight planets.

questions.prompt: How many planets are there in our solar system?
questions.explanation: There are eight planets: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.

questions.prompt: Which planet is often called the Red Planet?
questions.explanation: Mars looks red because iron minerals in its dirt have oxidised, or rusted.

questions.prompt: Which planet is most famous for its bright, wide rings?
questions.explanation: Saturn has the most spectacular rings, made of countless pieces of ice and rock.

questions.prompt: The Moon makes its own light.
questions.explanation: The Moon does not glow by itself. It shines because it reflects light from the Sun.

questions.prompt: Which planet is farthest from the Sun?
questions.explanation: Neptune is the eighth and most distant planet. Pluto is now called a dwarf planet.

questions.prompt: What is the Sun mostly made of?
questions.explanation: The Sun is a hot, glowing ball of hydrogen and helium gas at the centre of our solar system.

questions.prompt: Venus is the hottest planet in our solar system.
questions.explanation: Venus is wrapped in thick clouds that trap heat, making it the hottest planet.

questions.prompt: Which is the smallest planet in our solar system?
questions.explanation: Mercury is the smallest planet, only a little bigger than Earth's Moon.

questions.prompt: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
questions.explanation: Neil Armstrong stepped onto the Moon in July 1969 during the Apollo 11 mission.

questions.prompt: Which planet is third from the Sun?
questions.explanation: The order goes Mercury, Venus, then Earth. Earth is the only planet we know of with life.

questions.prompt: What is the giant storm on Jupiter called?
questions.explanation: The Great Red Spot is a swirling storm wider than Earth that has been raging for hundreds of years.

questions.prompt: Which planet spins tipped right over on its side?
questions.explanation: Uranus is tilted so far that it seems to roll around the Sun on its side.

questions.prompt: What kind of object is Pluto now called?
questions.explanation: In 2006 astronomers decided Pluto is a dwarf planet, because it is small and shares its path with lots of other icy objects.

questions.prompt: Pluto is bigger than Earth's Moon.
questions.explanation: Pluto is smaller than our Moon. It is only about two thirds as wide.

questions.prompt: Where is the asteroid belt?
questions.explanation: Most asteroids, rocky leftovers from when the planets formed, orbit the Sun in a belt between Mars and Jupiter.

questions.prompt: How many moons does Earth have?
questions.explanation: Earth has just one natural moon, which we simply call the Moon.

questions.prompt: What do we call a ball of ice and dust that grows a glowing tail when it nears the Sun?
questions.explanation: As a comet gets close to the Sun, its ice warms up and gives off gas and dust that stream out into a long tail.

questions.prompt: What are Saturn's rings mostly made of?
questions.explanation: Saturn's rings are made of billions of pieces of ice and rock, from tiny grains to chunks as big as a house.

questions.prompt: Mars has two small moons.
questions.explanation: Mars has two tiny moons called Phobos and Deimos.

questions.prompt: Which planet is closest in size to Earth?
questions.explanation: Venus is only a little smaller than Earth, which is why it is sometimes called Earth's twin.

questions.prompt: On Venus, one day is longer than one year.
questions.explanation: Venus spins very slowly. It takes longer to turn once than to travel all the way round the Sun.

questions.prompt: Which planet has the fastest winds in the solar system?
questions.explanation: Neptune's winds can blow at more than 2,000 kilometres per hour, faster than anywhere else in the solar system.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the galaxy our solar system belongs to?
questions.explanation: Our Sun is one of billions of stars in the Milky Way, a huge spiral galaxy.

questions.prompt: About how many Earth days does Mars take to travel once around the Sun?
questions.explanation: Mars is farther from the Sun than Earth, so its year is longer: about 687 Earth days.

questions.prompt: Neptune takes about how many Earth years to travel once around the Sun?
questions.explanation: Neptune is so far from the Sun that one trip around it takes about 165 Earth years.

questions.prompt: On average, about how many kilometres away is the Moon from Earth?
questions.explanation: The Moon is about 384,000 kilometres away. That is roughly 30 Earths lined up side by side.

questions.prompt: Which mission first landed people on the Moon in 1969?
questions.explanation: Apollo 11 landed on the Moon on 20 July 1969, and two astronauts walked on its surface.

questions.prompt: Who was the first person to travel into space?
questions.explanation: Yuri Gagarin orbited Earth in 1961 aboard a spacecraft called Vostok 1.

questions.prompt: The four planets closest to the Sun are mostly made of what?
questions.explanation: Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars are rocky planets. The four outer planets are much bigger and mostly gas or ice.

questions.prompt: What is a "shooting star" really?

options.label: A space rock burning up in our sky

questions.explanation: Shooting stars are meteors: small bits of space rock that heat up and glow as they rush through Earth's air.
